answer: Synchronous memory-hard puzzles deter Sybils by requiring agents to solve a fresh, beacon-seeded hash within a brief epoch window to stay registered. Because beacon seeding blocks precomputation and RAM-bound work prevents time-slicing, attackers must fund dedicated memory and power per identity. However, rented cloud clusters can still spawn parallel clones, while low-power nodes logging copper cargo at a harbor miss deadlines, making fixed difficulty a relic of symmetric hardware.
